name: Drab Grey
lede: Drab Grey is a light, warm, brownish grey from Ridgway's color atlases of 1886 and 1912, where *drab* means a dull, plain color with no brightness to it.

sections.title: From Ridgway to ISCC
sections.body: The swatch was first set down in Ridgway's *Nomenclature of Colors* of 1886, then carried into his 1912 atlas as plate XLVI, hue 17'''' [1]. The ISCC-NBS list of 1955 files it at block 79, and its nearest name there is "brownish pink", 3.7 units away [1]. On screen it reads as a warm grey, not a pink [1].

sections.title: Drab in the dictionary
sections.body: Paterson's dictionary gives *drab grey* in two descriptions. It describes mousy hair as having a drab grey or light brown color, and calls the word *quaker-coloured* a drab grey [2][3]. Both entries are about plain hair and plain dress. Related greys are [[grey]], [[warm-grey]], [[mouse-grey]] and [[taupe]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: It appears in 2,538 of 23,781 archive paintings, 10.67 per cent, commoner than 95 per cent of named colors [4]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light, in 42 per cent of the 1,800 paintings where it counts [4]. The 1100s peak, 8 of 50 paintings, rests on a thin early sample [4]. Willem van de Velde the Elder has it in 5 of 14 works here, 4.5 times the baseline [4]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so many warm greys are partly the effect of age [4].
